entities.name: Masjid Al-Huda
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
Masjid Al-Huda (مسجد الهدى, 'Mosque of Right Guidance') is a mosque in Singapore — one of the many mosques serving Singapore's Malay Muslim community that together form the infrastructure of Islamic religious life in one of Southeast Asia's most prosperous and religiously diverse city-states. The mosque's name, Al-Huda ('the guidance'), refers to the Quranic concept of divine guidance (huda), the direction toward truth and righteousness that Islam provides to believers.

Singapore's Muslim community has developed a distinctive form of modern, progressive Islam that has been studied globally as a model of Islam's accommodation to secular modernity: MUIS (the Islamic Religious Council) has developed fatwa (religious rulings) addressing distinctly modern questions — organ donation, reproductive technology, financial services, and the compatibility of Islamic practice with Singapore's secular legal system. The Muis Fatwa Committee has been particularly active in developing halal certification standards that now influence global food industry practice.

The mosque functions as a community hub beyond worship: Islamic education programs (madrasah), Quran classes, social welfare services, and zakat (charitable giving) distribution are all organized through Singapore's mosque network under MUIS coordination. The integration of traditional Islamic community functions with modern social service delivery reflects Singapore's distinctive approach to managing religious institutions as part of the broader social safety net.
